lines.text: Los Angeles to Washington, D.C. One hour, four minutes and twenty seconds.
March 1990. An SR-71 Blackbird, on its final flight.
Across the country, averaging about three thousand four hundred kilometres an hour.
It was built to cruise at more than three times the speed of sound, at up to eighty-five thousand feet.
That plane now belongs to the Smithsonian.
And the SR-71 still holds a record: the fastest crewed aircraft ever built with engines that breathe air.
But it is not the fastest aircraft ever flown.
So what beat it? That answer is a level of its own, and the full video is linked right here.
